evidence: ASN1Decoder.java:133-134 returns -1 for 0x80. readInteger (ASN1Decoder.java:71-72) passes -1 to read(int), where `new byte[length]` (line 170) throws NegativeArraySizeException, an unchecked exception instead of the declared IOException. So that half of the claim is right. The readSequence half is overstated. With length=-1 the while loop (line 57) is skipped and an empty list comes back, but the only caller, AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java:129-131, rejects it with an IOException ('Invalid sequence with size different to 2'). That is a graceful failure. The input is always a DER ECDSA signature, and DER (X.690 §10.1) forbids indefinite length, so valid input never hits this path. The only effect is that malformed input fails with a RuntimeException instead of an IOException. Making readLength throw IOException for 0x80 would be a cheap hardening fix, but it is not a functional bug.

AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java:114-115 call ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger) and ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger) and throw the results away. Lines 117-121 then build the same encoders again inside writeDerSeq(...). The two standalone lines do nothing except waste allocation and encoding work, so they should be removed.

ECDSAAlgorithmTest.java:42 builds a single KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC").genKeyPair() with the default curve: P-256 on JDK 17, the local JDK here, and P-384 on JDK 19+ per JDK-8267319. The same key is used for ES256, ES384 and ES512 (lines 59-72), so at least two of the three tests use a curve that does not match the algorithm. The tests still pass but miss real behaviour. If r/s are longer than signLength/2, integerToBytes (AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java:151-156) truncates them. The truncated values then round-trip consistently, so assertArrayEquals (line 56) passes even though data was lost. If r/s are shorter, they are only zero-padded. Neither case tests the realistic matched-curve path. Initialising the generator per algorithm with secp256r1, secp384r1 and secp521r1 (ECGenParameterSpec) would make the tests meaningful. This is a test-quality issue, not a production bug.
